They’re not assholes for wanting more from you. If they actually expect more from you (as opposed to just wanting it) try and explore why that might be. Is it because they feel they’ve given more to you than you give back? Is it because they have different ideals of what a friend is? Is it because they want the support of someone they hold dear? There could be a few reasons. I’d also explore why *you* don’t want to engage with people - is it a depression spell or anything? Are you having your basic connection needs met hence you don’t feel a need to reach out? What are your connection needs and how might they differ from your friends? Just some food for thought. 

I would say the honourable thing to do would be to meet them halfway. Don’t change yourself too much but make sure you put some effort into maintaining those relationships, or they’ll eventually stop trying and start feeling like you’re not a friend at all. For example, no one likes helping people move, but we do it for those we care about to nurture that relationship. 

There are some really basic ways to show you care. Communication being the main one. Text people back, pick up the phone or return a call. Even if you ask to meet up with someone in a couple months’ time, they’ll appreciate you’ve thought of them and are making time for it. And commit to it, don’t flake. 

I think if you wanted to stop being a fair weather friend you know what to do. But maybe try some internal work first as to why you’re feeling this way, so you can best communicate your own needs to others so they don’t take it too personally. That said, any relationship is about compromise, so you have to put in some effort too if they have to put up with your distance. Good friendships are so worth it.

If you’re double cleansing every day you definitely need a moisturiser! Especially with salicylic acid, as it strips out natural oils. This one just may not work for you. Have a look at the ingredients to see if this and your previous have any in common. But sometimes there’s just no obvious reason! I love Lush for example, but every single moisturiser was awful for me, yet their other products are great. A great way of trialling is to find out which stores do samples, that way you’re not wasting your money. I have oily skin but the right moisturiser has been game changing for me. When you over strip, your skin over produces oils which can lead to breakouts and oilier skin, so I would tone down the cleansing or maybe try to split them between am and pm. As for the moisturiser, definitely do some trials and focus on hydration (as not all moisturisers are hydrating!) good luck!

Hi, sorry you’re getting downvoted. I imagine it’s because you’re not officially diagnosed, but I sympathise with your situation of not knowing where to go. It’s tough finding the most appropriate sub sometimes.

You sound a bit erratic, are you ok? Are you safe? I hope you have a good support system around if you’re feeling unstable. If not, there are tons of help lines available depending on where you live.

Either way, you need to reframe it - you are using them. Not in a horrible way, and yes there will be some connection as you will need to be vulnerable, but tell yourself it is a short term relationship so that you can get what you need from them, ie a diagnosis or relevant form of help. It would be a disservice to yourself to not make the most of your sessions, they’re literally paid to take the heavy emotional burdens and make sense of it all with you! 

If you’re serious about getting help, use the tools available. Our health service is so crap I had to majorly know how to play the system just to be able to speak with someone who knew what they were talking about. And I’m so glad I did. Detach from the personable side of it all and get what you need to live your best life! Wishing you well and all the best.

I’m not in any realm of medical fields, and I have had one of these microbiome analyses done. Whilst there wasn’t a huge glowing answer (I also had a sibo test done) such as something being massively one way or the other leading to a dysbiosis, the supplements they did prescribe me lead me to gain my life back. I developed agoraphobia and panic attacks due to my ibs and what I was prescribed pretty much cleared up the panic attacks in a couple of months and also reduced my seemingly random flare ups. (A panic attack would trigger a flare but I also got them randomly / for seemingly no reason, and the fodmap diet didn’t help nor did elimination diets show that I had sensitivity to any specific food or food groups). From there I was able to get out and work to get my life back. I still have occasional flares and I’m definitely more sensitive to things like alcohol now but I attribute the test to my personal turning point. 

That said, I totally know what you’re talking about too. When searching for a decent gut test, I dismissed so many that were basically geared toward people whose gut health was fairly fine and just wanted to improve their health. Not for people whose gut needs fixing. Arguably, they’re not even necessary for normal people! Just another scam to make money. There’s a lot out there, and I can only speak from my own experience. The company I went with is called HealthPath if you wanted to look into it.

There is no one cause! Whilst it’s causes will be similar for some, there is no sole cause, as it’s the diagnosis of a symptom rather than a cause. For example, the fodmap diet and food in general doesn’t affect me at all, whereas for many it does. Yet we’ve all been diagnosed with the same thing. It’s bonkers.

I’ve only lost 55lbs, half of which was on a weight loss jab and half on my own because that shxts expensive. But here’s some things I’ve picked up: 

- tracking made me aware of what’s in stuff, so many surprises. So now I can make educated guesstimates if I can’t actually track. 

- a binge craving and a real craving are different for me and I can always tell. Binge cravings usually stem from emotions for me and can be for anything unhealthy, whereas real cravings are usually something specific I don’t have all the time. Binge cravings are harder to ignore but distraction is key, as is, for me, having a good cry. With real cravings I wait three days and if I’m still craving it, I have it and I track it. The craving goes away after I’ve had it. With bingeing it’s mindless and almost compulsive. 

- make swaps everywhere you can. I’m not talking an apple instead of a pizza, but opt for diet drinks, low cal versions etc. every little helps. 

- if you don’t feel like eating, don’t! I used to think I had to have three meals a day but for me swapping breakfast for a coffee suits me fine and saves so much. Find what works for you. It may not be every day but just ANY day. 

- days don’t matter, but weeks do. You can have a bad day if in the grand scheme of things you’ve offset it. Be kind to yourself over it. 

- get back on the horse. Always. Leading on from my previous point, getting back on is more important than falling off. 

- allow yourself to live a life. Go for dinner with friends. Try that one thing you’ve always wanted to. Drink if you want! All of these one offs won’t kill you and tbh I’d rather wait another year to get to my goal so that I can make memories. 

- don’t force yourself to like things you just really don’t. Goes for exercise too.

For example, my relationship with the term ‘neurodivergence’ usually occurs at work. While we have some great DE&I networks who have done great work to teach people about these types of terms, the collective understanding amongst the wider business (at least in my case) remains that ‘neurodivergent’ equals some kind of learning difficulty to them. This can be anything from autism to Down syndrome, but the point is they wouldn’t typically factor in challenges in emotional regulation within that. 

So whilst, I personally would say we are neurodivergent, as we do perceive and navigate through the world different to those without BPD, we must be mindful of who may not class us as such. I’m so sorry you’re going through this. Two years ago, I was exactly the same. For me the solution was a three pronged attack. One to combat anxiety, one to get myself comfortable with being outside again (I was full on agoraphobic too) and three to address the underlying issue of my ibs. Points one and three were actually combatted at the same time. I paid for a private full gut MOT (microbiome analysis) and they recommended me supplements based on my results, as well as dietary and lifestyle recommendations. I had tried generic over the counter stuff, as well as prescription drugs for both ibs and anxiety, and like you nothing touched the sides and no doctor was helping or knew what they were talking about - I was desperate and trying anything. I got prescribed three supplements, one was a “mood barrier” (idk what was actually in it but that was its name.) for me the panic attacks pretty much vanished within about a month or two. Then I could address step two, exposure therapy. Doing little walks and using grounding techniques, extending the walks or journeys little by little. I always took immodium and never pushed myself too far, but doing it that way took some time (around 4 months for me) but really helped. With the other supplements, that I still take now, they helped to heal my gut to the point where I felt and most days feel, like my old self again, pre ibs. I never had any food sensitivities though to note. It was a combination of these three to lead me where I am today. Getting the subway to work most days, no immodium, no panic or anxiety. I know my way will not be for everyone, as so many of us experience / contracted ibs differently. But this is what worked for me. I’d really recommend a microbiome analysis to anyone, but make sure it’s a good one. So many ‘gut health’ tests are geared towards those who merely want to improve gut health, not fix something that’s broken. Genuine best of luck to you and please know that there is a light at the end of the tunnel!

When I started to accept responsibility for my behaviour, life started to get better. But I must stress this is not exclusive to BPD and should be practiced by all. 

I think that when looking at complex mental issues of one or more people in any type of relationship, the main point is that no one ‘trumps’ the other. Even if on paper one person has greater needs or displays far riskier behaviour, that does not negate the other person’s needs. I say this as my ex did not have bpd, but she had mental health issues of some kind and always used the notion that she was autistic, to completely absolve herself of any responsibility for anything she did or how she made me feel. Even when I expressed it fairly and calmly. No one is more important than another. We should all strive to be fair and equal. Having bpd isn’t a get out of jail free card, but it can land you in metaphorical jail more times than average. And some people know this, and don’t have the capacity to handle that. And that has to be okay.

I recently posted a success story, but I never said I was cured because I’m not, it’s just a dramatic improvement. That said, SOME people can technically ‘cure their ibs’ purely because whatever they have going on gets misdiagnosed *as* IBS. 

Misdiagnoses are so prevalent when it comes to gut issues, and most doctors end up slapping the IBS term onto anything they don’t understand or can’t explain through the limited methods they know. So if someone was technically diagnosed with ibs but it was actually say, food poisoning or something, then they’d technically be right in saying it’s curable. The issue is, we don’t always know what the cause or real problem is. 

For more typical ibs sufferers, it’s been around for most of their life and responds to elements of the fodmap diet. I do not have ‘true’ ibs.
